Mirra.what: Follow X accounts from Telegram: every post arrives in minutes, and a short brief tells you what each author has been saying and how it changed.
arch: Ingest claims a handle, not a feed — one paid fetch per author per cycle is shared by every subscriber tracking them, each re-applying its own content filter and time window

Four dedup layers guard an upstream that returns wrong authors and out-of-window posts: client-side author validation, timestamp validation with clock-skew tolerance, a 30-day seen-set, and a Snowflake-id tiebreaker because upstream timestamps are only second-precision
Document packs are frozen and numbered before any model call, then shuffled — sorting by views buries the low-engagement tail in the part of the context window models attend to least
One model call per author per window; clustering, importance scoring, shortlist selection and citation verification are all code, not tokens
Continuity rides on the previous edition's own grounded output rather than re-fetched posts, and a recurrence claim is downgraded unless its cited evidence appears verbatim in today's text
proc: The live prompt is a versioned database row, not code — a change ships as a new version and is measured against the one it replaces
Retry logic is branched on evidence: half of all parse failures sat exactly at the output-token cap, so a plain re-roll would have been inert for the majority case
A lint canary injects a violation on every commit and fails if the rule does not catch it, because a dead rule and a clean tree exit identically
Staging and production are separate deploy paths released on the operator's call, and user-facing copy is banked and approved before it ships

Social Hook.what: It watches your development work and turns it into social posts in your voice — approved by you, or fully autonomous.
arch: The commit hook backgrounds itself so a commit is never blocked, and unregistered repositories, off-branch commits and CI environments exit before any model call

One abstract adapter contract applied four times over — publishing platforms, media generators, messaging channels and model providers — so adding a platform is one factory function and one registration, never a branch in a dispatch chain
Callers branch on a platform's declared capabilities rather than its name, so a platform without threads or native quoting degrades to a link instead of failing

Five model providers behind one normalised response type; the Claude CLI provider embeds its JSON schema in the system prompt instead of using structured-output mode, which forces a multi-turn validation loop costing three or more round trips

Four gates stand between an approved draft and a live post — no adapter, no credentials, a format that cannot be auto-posted, and unresolved media — each holding the draft editable rather than failing it
proc: A wiring check treats a capability with no caller as unbuilt. It exists because the first live run found 112 functions that were complete, unit-tested and reachable from nothing — reviews are scoped to diffs, and a diff cannot show an absent caller
Allowlist entries in that check require a written reason; a blank reason fails the build, and bulk allowlisting is not permitted
Releases are cut from conventional commits automatically, and CLI documentation is regenerated in CI and fails the build if it differs from what is committed
Concurrent agents share one database, so a test count only counts when measured from a clean checkout inside a quiescence window — the project quotes members, never totals

Live on X and LinkedIn, built to add more platforms

Clauded.what: Claude Code running inside a Docker sandbox: skip permission prompts safely while clipboard, sound, Chrome, git and MCP still reach your Mac.
arch: Bridges are ordinary local HTTP services on the Mac that container-side shims call by name: pbcopy, pbpaste, xdg-open and the sound player are replaced with clients that detect the container and fall back to the real binary when run natively

The microphone bridge runs the other way — the host streams 16 kHz raw PCM into a container FIFO exposed as an audio source, and the client only opens the socket while that source is actually recording, so the Mac microphone runs during capture rather than for the whole session
Consent for capture is anchored host-side: a native dialog defaulting to Deny, a timeout that resolves to denied, a per-session cache, and a cooldown so a retrying client cannot produce a prompt loop

Every bridge request carries a token compared in constant time, and the container never holds an API key — authentication is the normal browser login, with credentials living in a mounted host directory
An opt-in firewall drops egress by default and re-admits only the model API, the code host, two package registries and telemetry
proc: The changelog is a single append-only numbered list, never renumbered, so an entry number stays a stable reference; entries state symptom, root cause and fix
A working bridge was deleted once its premise proved false — Claude in Chrome pairs over a cloud relay rather than localhost, so the Mac-side proxy had never been necessary
The build stopped pruning Docker images system-wide after it was found deleting other projects' images, and the deliberate non-use is recorded in a comment so it is not reintroduced
The Linux port is published as an assessment rather than started: three hard blockers and four degraded features named, with the parts already portable listed so they are not re-audited

Five bridges hand back the conveniences: clipboard, sound, Chrome, git, MCP
Consent for anything sensitive stays on the Mac, with deny-by-default dialogs
Run as many sessions in parallel as you like

LikeWiki.what: Your X likes, compiled into a private wiki: every claim cites the post it came from, and the pages rebuild themselves nightly.
arch: Source pages are the append-mostly record and are read-only to every agent: the body holds the full transcript and media descriptions and routinely exceeds a model's read cap, so rewriting one from a capped read would silently truncate it
Concept pages cite sources and never other concept pages, because sources are stable while concept pages are rewritten as new material lands

There is no database. Flat markdown in git is the store, and the reading surface never touches the working tree — each request pins one commit and reads every page from that revision, so an ingest run landing mid-request cannot produce a torn read
Tags, source counts and index ordering are computed by inverting the citation map, so the model owns judgement and nothing else: a tag is by construction a page that really does cite the source
A read-only server exposes the catalogue, page summaries, source search and raw sources to other agents, every response stamped with the commit and its age so a stale checkout announces itself
proc: Video ingest verifies magic bytes after download. A field-name mismatch had been saving thumbnail images under a video filename, so a single still was described as if it covered a two-hour talk — 40 source pages were invalidated before the mismatch was spotted
That fix was silently reverted by a later refactor and re-landed with a measurement: 57 of 58 affected videos were recoverable from URLs already stored
Grounding audits are owed by content fingerprint rather than commit history, so a page audited in one month and extended the next is owed another — the previous heuristic counted it as done
Rewriting agents reported their own work clean; 24 independent adversarial auditors then found six real defects they had missed, including an attribution to the wrong speaker entirely

Track Record.what: Public predictions, kept honest: every call goes into a ledger, gets tracked to its outcome, and scores the person who made it.
arch: A dedicated extraction run over a document pack that already exists — one additional model call against a versioned prompt, and no new capture pipeline
The ledger is a typed scoring contract over an open payload: everything the model returns is stored losslessly, and only the fields a resolver or a filter computes on are typed

Subjects are canonical at creation and never free text — tickers for equities, series identifiers for macro, coin identifiers for crypto, knowledge-base identifiers for people and policies, and an author-local subject when nothing matches, so capture never blocks

The three clocks partition the open set: market data resolves anything carrying a spec, the author's own subsequent posts resolve the roughly 60% of calls that carry no time signal at all, and policy caps only what never had a horizon
Claims are immutable — a restatement annotates and a revision opens a new linked segment, so an author can never walk back an entry — and price anchors are captured once at insert, never recomputed
proc: Only facts are stored; verdicts including the score are render-layer and versioned, so the formula can change without rewriting history

Resolution rate is instrumentation, never scoreboard: what counts as checkable is partly the classifier's judgement on marginal cases, so a public percentage would move whenever the extractor is revised
The classification vocabulary is itself a versioned row — every labelled example stamps the version it was labelled under, and a change ships as a new version with notes rather than an edit
A call that reaches its horizon unresolved is graded against the relevant index, never scored as a miss and never dropped, because dropping it is the cherry-pick the product exists to expose

Claude Historian.what: Makes past Claude Code sessions searchable — what was tried, what worked, what was decided. My contribution took search from 45% to 100% of history.
arch: No index, no database and no background process — transcripts are streamed from disk per query, with a file-level pre-filter running before anything is parsed as JSON
Files under 400 KB are read whole and split, larger ones are streamed line by line, and the crossover was benchmarked rather than assumed
Ranking is two-stage: a per-message term score, then a multiplicative refinement with capped match boosting that replaced an inverse-document-frequency computation the corpus did not justify

The coverage fix walks project directories recursively and rolls subagent hits up to their parent session with per-agent hit counts — one result per subagent was rejected because a single session had spawned 1,239 of them

Subagent directories are named after their parent session, so recursive discovery had to be preceded by a real session resolver, or a request to summarise a session would silently return one subagent instead
proc: The repository had no behavioural tests, so an evaluation harness was built before anything was changed — each fixture asserting one direction only and pinned at session level, so a later change in result shape cannot break the assertion

Phases were ordered by dependency rather than by value: recursive discovery more than doubles the bytes scanned, so it could not land before the scan was made cheaper, and a raw-byte case-insensitive pre-filter measured 3.7 times faster than a lowercased-copy scan on identical results

A full-text sidecar index was designed and then cancelled — session-scoped search alone took the reported complaint from 6,500 ms to 4 ms, while the sidecar bought latency only on global search at the cost of a plaintext copy of every conversation
One negative result was kept in the record: a hand-written character-code fold ran about 50% slower than the native lowercase on line matching, so raw bytes win only where they avoid a decode

Xactions.what: A full X operations suite an AI agent can drive — publishing, analytics, audience CRM, monitoring and autonomous personas, through one MCP surface.
arch: Three data paths behind one tool surface — a stealth-configured browser, direct calls to the platform's own internal endpoints, and nine interchangeable engine adapters
Authentication is a session cookie rather than a developer key, so the tool surface is as wide as the account holder's own reach rather than as narrow as an API tier

An autonomous persona is a long-lived loop, not a cron job: an activity pattern decides whether it should be awake at all, a strategy sets daily ceilings on follows, likes, comments and posts, and each session's budget is jittered so activity does not land on a machine-readable rhythm
Streams are durable polling — repeatable queue jobs against a pooled browser, with a per-stream lock preventing overlapping polls and exponential backoff on consecutive failures
Bulk operations clear four gates before anything executes: a blacklist, per-action daily caps, a refusal above a hundred actions without an explicit override, and a resumable progress file
proc: The article extractor's boundary-stripping was lifted out of the browser closure into a plain module for one reason — a closure that exists only inside a page evaluation cannot be referenced from a test

Query identifiers for internal endpoints rotate upstream and fail silently, returning nothing while everything visible still works, so the fix shipped with the diagnosis rather than just the new value
Scraping tools that existed only as uncommitted working-tree changes were committed, because a clean reinstall would have removed a dependency another project was built on

Stellar Explorer.what: An explorable 3D map of the night sky: fly between 117k stars, open any into a detail view, with sound tied to the journey.
arch: One hand-written shader program serves every body — three procedural surface functions blended by step masks on a type uniform, so there is no branch in the fragment path and no second program to compile
Moons do not exist until their planet is expanded, and are fully released on collapse: geometry, materials and children are walked and disposed rather than hidden
A five-pass composite over a tone-mapped render at a capped pixel ratio — bloom, then vignette, chromatic aberration and film grain, the last three written by hand
The background is procedural too: three counter-rotating point shells with additive nebula sprites drawn to canvas at runtime, so depth and parallax cost no texture assets and no network fetch
Hover raycasting is throttled to 20 Hz and hits are routed by user-data tagging, so a single cast distinguishes a click on a body from a click on the void that body becomes
proc: Interaction feel was tuned before features were added: orbits freeze on hover and in detail view, and the camera offsets its target so the body sits off-centre with room for the reading panel

Audio is synthesised rather than loaded from files, and the one audible cue is the one whose gain envelope peaks together with its noise buffer — the others are inaudible by measurement rather than missing by omission
